question: Can a DDPM-trained model be sampled in far fewer steps, with comparable quality, by changing the generative process rather than retraining?
hypothesis: A family of non-Markovian forward processes shares the DDPM training objective, so a pretrained DDPM can be sampled with a deterministic, shorter trajectory without retraining.
contributions: Generalise DDPMs to non-Markovian forward processes that share the same L1 training objective (Theorem 1)
DDIM: the sigma=0 deterministic case, an implicit model usable with pretrained DDPMs
Accelerated sampling over a sub-sequence tau of timesteps, 10x to 50x faster
Consistency, latent interpolation and low-error reconstruction from x_T

method.summary: Defines a family of inference processes q_sigma with the same marginals as DDPM, giving generative updates indexed by sigma (eta). Sets sigma=0 for deterministic DDIM and samples over a sub-sequence of the 1000 timesteps, using existing DDPM checkpoints (and one self-trained CelebA model).
method.task: unconditional image generation (sampler change for diffusion models)

models.name: DDPM U-Net eps_theta
models.architecture: U-Net based on Wide ResNet, as Ho et al. 2020
models.init_from: pretrained DDPM checkpoints for CIFAR10, Bedroom, Church

other.CelebA: own model trained with L1; five feature map resolutions from 64x64 to 4x4

inference.decoding: DDIM update (Eq. 12) with sigma_tau_i(eta) = eta*sqrt((1-a_{i-1})/(1-a_i))*sqrt(1-a_i/a_{i-1}); eta=0 is DDIM, eta=1 is DDPM; sigma-hat is DDPM with larger noise std
inference.samples: FID sample count not stated; one trained model per dataset, no seeds stated

parameters.tau selection: quadratic tau_i=floor(c*i^2) for CIFAR10, linear tau_i=floor(c*i) for the rest
parameters.interpolation: spherical linear interpolation of two x_T, DDIM dim(tau)=50

metrics.name: Reconstruction error
metrics.definition: per-dimension mean squared error, scaled to [0,1], encode x0 to xT then decode with S steps, CIFAR-10 test set

metrics.name: Sampling time
metrics.definition: hours to sample 50k images on one Nvidia 2080 Ti

eval.protocol: Single table per setting; no seeds, intervals or significance tests stated.
